content:
The goal of #36983 was to add two lemmas that say that the permutation group on a type with at most two elements is cyclic. There was however no good place for this (except by themselves in a new file) because of the conflicting interaction between

  • assert_not_exists Field that is needed in Data/Finite/Perm
  • the use of tactics (gcongr, positivity) in GroupAction/SpecificGroups/Cyclic

For this, I was led to split GroupAction/SpecificGroups/Cyclicinto two files, its first part becasme GroupAction/SpecificGroups/Cyclic/Basic and can impose assert_not_exists Field, and the remainder of the original file that I kept in place (so that no modification of other import are needed).

However, I am not sure that this is the correct way to do, and I wanted to point out the above-evoked between assert_not_exists and the use of tactics. Probably better solutions will be proposed here.

@Antoine Chambert-Loir I think such a split is welcome. For the sake of git history, would you mind splitting this into 2 PRs? One that only moves things around, and another which adds the two lemmas?

I think that having more files is fine. On the other hand in my opinion we should have files, made only of import lines that allow to import reasonable part of the library (like "I will need commutative algebra in my project, what should I import?) and document this somehow.
@Riccardo Brasca, I am not sure I understand what you mean in your second sentence.

Nothing related to your PR. It was just an idea to make it easier to new contributors to import all "commutative algebra" in one go (we often have people that only import Defs files and then struggle because of missing instances and so on).
We already have one such file: import Mathlib
